# SigLIP v1 Zero-Shot E2E Notebook — Review fixes

**Review:** `siglip_v1_zero_shot_colab_Review.md` (5 October 2026; reviewed commit `3641985`, unchanged on `main`)
**Notebook:** `tutorials/siglip_v1_zero_shot_colab.ipynb`, regenerated by `tools/build_notebook.py` (`build_notebook.py/2.2`)
**Readiness:** **Verification pending** — the fixes are verified offline only; a hosted one-pass Run all is still required.
**Status labels:** unchanged. `STATUS.md`, `docs/release-verification.md` and the registry are left for the maintainer.

Every change is made in the generator, the template or the carried package; the notebook is regenerated and
`--check` is clean. The default path is unchanged in what it computes (same data, split, baselines, training
configuration and exports); what changed on it is how the runtime is installed, the guided layer, and that quality
outcomes are printed and recorded as verdicts instead of asserted.

### Additional observation (not a review finding; not changed)

While tracing SIG-M2, `adapt` was found to select the kept epoch on **validation accuracy** (`best_score`/`current`
read `entry["val"]["accuracy"]`), whereas its docstring, the notebook prose, `docs/release-verification.md` and the
adapter's `selection` string say **validation text-to-image mAP**. Changing the selector would change the default
path's results, so it is left for the maintainer; the new guided text avoids naming the selector metric.

The review's BYOD minimum (P4b: 12 photographs) counted only `split_dataset`. The notebook also validated every split
with the eight-record floor, which would have refused a 12-photograph set at the test split; the per-split floor is
now one record for validation and test, so 12 is the true end-to-end minimum.

## User-visible changes

- Section 1 is now one collapsed infrastructure cell that builds (or reuses) `dimer_isolated_env_<lock digest>/` and
  routes later cells to it; nothing is installed into the kernel and Run all needs no restart. The first run downloads
  the locked PyTorch CUDA stack into that folder (several GB), as the in-kernel install did. Linux x86_64 only.
- New committed file `tutorials/requirements-colab.lock.txt` (47 packages, hashes for manylinux x86_64).
- Section 6 and Section 8 print verdicts instead of asserting; `evaluation_report.json` and `result.json` gain
  `comparison.verdicts`.
- `SiglipPipeline.adapt` always starts from the pinned base (previously it continued from the current weights); the
  adapter record and artifact manifest gain `started_from`. New public `SiglipPipeline.restore_base()` and
  `min_byod_photographs()`.
- BYOD: new `BYOD_PATH` field; the stated minimum is 12 photographs for two labels (was "at least eight");
  `split_dataset` now refuses a split that leaves a label without a training or validation photograph; refusals name
  the `labels.csv` line and file.
- New optional Section 10 (off by default) and the guided layer; the "Optional experiments" paragraph now points to it.
- Generator `build_notebook.py/2.2` (shared with the other notebooks of this template); a template without the new keys
  renders exactly as /2 did apart from the generator version string.

(7,087,872 parameters per vision block, float32).

3. The REL12 BYOD journey: one compatible and one incompatible zip, through `BYOD_PATH` (Kaggle or Jupyter) and
